errors.text: The hypothesis emphasizes Ostwald ripening and growth of larger irregular aggregates, whereas the target mechanism centers on Au/Cu surface segregation followed by shell melting and evaporation, producing an overall particle-size reduction and elliptical-to-spherical reshaping.
It identifies Au and Pt as the surface-segregating species rather than the observed Au and Cu.

The proposed breakdown boundary is an unsupported size threshold with presumed recovery above 20 nm, while the demonstrated boundary is primarily temperature-dependent, becoming important above approximately 673 K, with additional size and shape dependence.
